translations.text: The word of the Lord that came to Hosea son of Beeri in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel.

The beginning of the Lord’s words to Hosea. The Lord said to Hosea, “Go, take for yourself a wife of prostitution and children of prostitution, for the land will prostitute itself completely, turning away from the Lord.”
He went and took Gomer daughter of Diblaim, and she conceived and bore him a son.

The Lord said to him, “Call his name Jezreel, for in a little while I will exact punishment from the house of Jehu for the bloodshed of Jezreel, and I will put an end to the kingdom of the house of Israel.”
And on that day I will break Israel’s bow in the valley of Jezreel.
She conceived again and bore a daughter, and he said to him, “Call her name Not Pitied, for I will no longer have pity on the house of Israel, but will oppose them with hostility.”
“But I will have pity on the children of Judah and save them through the Lord their God. I will not save them by bow, sword, or war, nor by chariots, horses, or horsemen.”
She weaned Not Pitied, then conceived again and bore a son.
He said, “Call his name Not My People, for you are not my people, and I am not yours.”

The number of the children of Israel was like the sand of the sea, beyond measure and beyond counting. And in the place where it was said to them, “You are not my people,” there they will be called “Children of the living God.”
The children of Judah and the children of Israel will be gathered together, and they will appoint one ruler for themselves and come up from that land, for great is the day of Jezreel.
Say to your brother, “My People,” and to your sister, “Pitied.”
“Contend with your mother, contend with her, for she is not my wife, and I am not her husband. I will remove her prostitution from before my face and her adultery from between her breasts,
“for I will strip her naked and make her as she was on the day of her birth. I will make her like a wilderness and set her like a waterless land, and I will kill her with thirst.
“I will have no pity on her children, for they are children of prostitution.

“For their mother prostituted herself, and she who bore them acted shamefully. She said, ‘I will go after my lovers, who will give me my bread and water, my clothing and linen, my wine and oil, and everything I need.’
“Therefore I will block her roads with barriers and dig ditches across her roads, so that she cannot find her paths.
“She will run after her lovers but will not reach them; she will seek them but will not find them. Then she will say, ‘I will go and return to my first husband, for I was better off then than now.’
“She did not know that I gave her the grain, wine, and oil, and multiplied silver for her. She made silver objects and multiplied gold objects for Baal.
“Therefore I will turn back and take away my grain in its season, and my wine and oil in their seasons. I will take back from her my clothing and linen, so that she cannot cover her nakedness.
“Now I will expose her impurity before her lovers, and no one will rescue her from my hands.
“I will put an end to all her merriment, her festivals, her new moons, her Sabbaths, and all her fairs.

“I will destroy her vineyards and fig trees, of which she once said, ‘These are my payments, which my lovers gave me.’ I will make them a testimony, and the wild beasts of the wilderness, the birds of the sky, and the creeping creatures of the earth will devour them.
“I will exact vengeance from her for the days of the Baals, when she sacrificed to them, put on earrings and her necklaces, and went after her lovers, forgetting me,” says the Lord.
Therefore, look, I will lead her astray and make her like a wilderness, and I will speak to her heart.

And from there I will give her her possessions and the valley of Achor to open her understanding. She will humble herself there as in the days of her youth and as in the days when she came out of the land of the Egyptians.
And on that day, says the Lord, she will call me “My husband,” and she will not call me “Baalim.”
And I will remove the names of the Baalim from her mouth, and their names will no longer be remembered.

And on that day I will make a covenant for them with the beasts of the wilderness, the birds of heaven, and the creeping creatures of the earth. I will destroy bow, sword, and battle from the land, and I will make you dwell securely.
And I will betroth you to myself forever. I will betroth you to myself in righteousness and justice, in mercy and compassion.
And I will betroth you to myself in faithfulness, and you will know the Lord.
And on that day, says the Lord, I will answer the heavens, and the heavens will answer the earth.
And the earth will answer the grain, the wine, and the oil, and they will answer Jezreel.
And I will sow her for myself upon the earth, and I will have mercy on the one who received no mercy, and I will say to the one who was not my people,
“You are my people.” And he will say, “Lord, you are my God.”
And the Lord said to me, “Go again and love a woman who loves evil and is an adulteress, just as God loved the children of Israel, while they looked to foreign gods and loved raisin cakes.”
And I hired her for myself for fifteen pieces of silver, one cor of barley, and one mar of wine.
And I say to her, “You shall remain with me for many days. You shall no longer prostitute yourself, and you shall no longer belong to another man.”
For the children of Israel will remain for many days without a king, without a ruler, without sacrifices, without an altar, without a priesthood, and without revelations.
And afterward the children of Israel will return and seek the Lord their God and David their king, and they will be strengthened in the Lord and in his goodness in the last days.
Hear the word of the Lord, children of Israel, for the Lord has a case against the inhabitants of the land, because there is no truth, no mercy, and no knowledge of God upon the earth.
Cursing, lying, murder, theft, and adultery have spread over the land, and bloodshed mingles with bloodshed.

Therefore the land will mourn and grow faint, together with all its inhabitants, the beasts of the wilderness, the creatures that crawl on the earth, and the birds of the heavens; and the fish of the sea will disappear.
For there is no one to bring a charge and no one to rebuke, but my people are like a priest who opposes.
And they will grow weak by day, and the prophet too will grow weak with you. I have made your mother like the night.

My people became like someone who had no knowledge. Because you rejected knowledge, I too will reject you, so that you will no longer serve as priest to me. And because you forgot the law of your God, I too will forget your children.
As they increased in number, so they sinned against me. I will turn their glory into dishonor.
They will feed on the sins of my people and give themselves over to their own wrongdoing.
And as it is with the people, so it shall be with the priest. I will exact vengeance from him according to his ways, and repay him according to his intentions.
They will eat but will not be satisfied. They have prostituted themselves but will not prosper, because they abandoned the Lord to give themselves indiscriminately to prostitution.
And the heart of my people embraced wine and drunkenness.
They sought answers through lots, and with his rods they told him. In this way they were led astray into prostitution and prostituted themselves away from their God.

They offered sacrifices on the mountaintops and slaughtered offerings on the hills, beneath oaks, aspens, and leafy trees, because their shade seemed pleasant. Therefore your daughters will prostitute themselves, and your daughters-in-law will commit adultery.

And I will not punish your daughters when they prostitute themselves, or your daughters-in-law when they commit adultery, because they themselves mingled with prostitutes and offered sacrifices with those who were consecrated. And your people, who did not understand this, mingled with prostitutes.
But you, Israel, do not be ignorant; and you, Judah, do not enter Gilgal or go up to the house of On, and do not swear, “As the Lord lives.”
For Israel has become to me like a heifer that throws off the yoke. Now the Lord will pasture them like a lamb in a quiet place.
Ephraim is a partner of idols; he set a stumbling block for himself. They desired the idols of the Canaanites; they all loved wine. Leave him alone.
They committed prostitution shamelessly; they loved dishonor in his pride.
A whirlwind will blow into his wings, and they will be ashamed of their altars.

Hear this, priests, and pay attention, house of Israel; listen, royal household, for judgment is against you, because you became a snare for the watchtower and like a net spread over the summit of the height,
which hunters set for the hunt. I am the one who disciplines you.
I know Ephraim, and Israel is not hidden from me, for now Ephraim has committed prostitution, and Israel has become defiled.
They did not direct their thoughts toward returning to their God, for a spirit of prostitution is in them, and they did not know the Lord.
Israel’s pride will be humbled before his face, and Israel and Ephraim will falter in their lawlessness; Judah too will falter with them.
They will go with bulls and offerings to seek the Lord, but they will not find him, because he has withdrawn from them.
For they abandoned the Lord, because foreign children were born to them. Now [?] will devour them and their allotted lands.
Blow the trumpet on the hills; shout on the heights; proclaim in the house of On, “Benjamin has become foolish.”
And Ephraim became a ruin in the days of rebuke. Among the tribes of Israel I showed my faithfulness.
The rulers of Judah became like those who move boundaries. I will pour out my onslaught upon them like water.
Ephraim deprived his adversary and trampled on justice, because he began to follow worthless things.
And I will be like a disturbance to Ephraim and like a sting to the house of Judah.
Ephraim saw his sickness, and Judah his pains. Ephraim went to the Assyrians and sent messengers to King Jareb, but he could not save you or relieve you of your pains.
For I am like a leopard against Ephraim and like a lion against the house of Judah. I will attack and seize them; I will carry them away, and there will be no one to rescue them.
I will go and return to my place until they are brought to ruin and seek my face. In their distress they will come early to me.
And they will say, “Let us return and go to the Lord our God, for he struck us, and he himself will heal us; he wounded us, and he will bind us up.
He will revive us after two days, and on the third day we will rise and live before him.
Let us know him, and let us press on to know the Lord. We will find him ready like the dawn, and he will come to us like the early and late rain upon the earth.”
What shall I do with you, Ephraim, or how shall I deal with you, Judah? For your mercy is like a morning cloud and like the morning dew that passes away.
Therefore I cut down your prophets and killed them with the word of my mouth, and your judgments will shine forth like light.
For I desire mercy, not sacrifice, and knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.
And they became like someone who transgresses a covenant. Now Gilead has despised me.
A city that does worthless things and stirs up the waters.
And the priests hid your strength like that of a robber. They killed Shechem on the road, for they committed lawlessness.
In the house of Israel I saw horrors. Now Ephraim has prostituted itself, and Israel has been defiled.
And Judah began harvesting when I restored the captives of my people.
When I heal Israel, the evils of Ephraim and the evils of Samaria will be revealed, for they practiced falsehood. A thief will enter it, and a robber will strip people on its roads.
For they will murmur together, as they murmur in their minds. I remembered all their evil deeds. Now their own schemes have surrounded them; they have come before my face.
With their evil deeds they made the king glad, and with their falsehood the princes.
They are all adulterers, like an oven kindled for baking, blazing from the flame and from the lump of fat until it is leavened.
In the days of your kings, the princes began to rage from wine, and they stretched out their hands with evildoers.
For their hearts blazed like a furnace when cursing them. All night Ephraim was filled with sleep. Morning came, and they blazed like a flame of fire.
They all grew hot like a blazing furnace, and fire consumed their judges. All their kings fell, and none of them called upon me.
Ephraim mingled with the peoples, and Ephraim became a cake that had not been turned over.
Foreigners consumed his strength, and he did not know it. His gray hairs blossomed, and he did not notice.
And Israel's pride will be humbled to his face. Yet they did not return to the Lord their God, nor did they seek him in all this.
And Ephraim was like a senseless dove without understanding. They sought encouragement in Egypt and went to the Assyrians.
Wherever they go, I will cast my net over them and bring them down like the birds of heaven. I will discipline them with the report of their distress.
Woe to them, for they fled from me! They are miserable, for they acted wickedly against me. I redeemed them, but they spoke falsely against me.
Their hearts did not cry out to me; instead, they wailed on their beds. Over grain and wine they [?]. They were disciplined by me.
And I strengthened their arms, but they plotted evil against me.

They turned to nothing and became like a drawn bow. Their princes will fall by the sword because of their lack of discipline and the harshness of their tongues, for this is their folly in the land of the Egyptians.
In their lap, like the earth, and like an eagle over the house of the Lord, because they transgressed my covenant and acted wickedly against my laws.
They will cry out to me, “God, we have known you!”
For Israel turned away from good; they pursued the enemy.
They made themselves kings, but not through me; they ruled, but did not tell me. They made their silver and gold into idols for themselves, so that they might perish.
Smash your calf, Samaria! My fury has flared up against them. How long will they be unable to cleanse themselves in Israel?
And a carpenter made it, and it is not God, for your calf, Samaria, leads people astray.
For they sowed what was scorched by the hot wind, and their destruction will receive it. Their crop will not produce meal; even if it does, foreigners will eat it.
Israel has been engulfed; now he has become like a useless vessel among the nations.
For they went to the Assyrians. Ephraim rejoiced alone; he loved bribes.
Therefore they will be handed over among the nations. But now I will receive them, and they will cease for a little while from anointing kings and rulers.
For Ephraim multiplied altars, and his beloved altars became a cause of sin for him.
I will write many things concerning them, and his ordinances were regarded as foreign things.

The beloved altars—for even if they offer sacrifices and eat the meat, the Lord will not accept it. Now he will remember their injustices and exact punishment for their lawless deeds. They returned to Egypt, and among the Assyrians they will eat unclean things.
For Israel forgot his Maker, and they built shrines. Judah multiplied fortified cities. I will send fire into his cities, and it will consume their foundations.
Do not rejoice, Israel, and do not be glad like the peoples of the earth, for you have prostituted yourself away from your God. You loved bribes on every threshing floor of grain.
Threshing floors and winepresses did not recognize them, and wine failed them.
They will not dwell in the Lord’s land. Ephraim will dwell in Egypt, and among the Assyrians they will eat unclean things.

They did not offer wine to the Lord, and their sacrifices did not please him. They will be like mourners’ bread to them: everyone who eats it will become unclean. For their bread will be for themselves, and it must not enter the Lord’s house.
What will you do on the days of the annual celebration and on the days of the Lord’s feast?

Therefore, behold, they will go into the misery of the Egyptians. Memphis will receive them, and Michmash will bury them. Destruction will inherit their silver, and thorns will grow in their dwellings.

The days of your punishment have arrived; the days of your repayment have arrived. Israel will be afflicted like a crazed prophet, like a man possessed by a demon. Because of the multitude of your injustices, error has multiplied.
Ephraim is a watchman with God. The prophet is a snare that causes stumbling on all his paths. They planted error in the house of God.
They became corrupt as in the days of the high places. He will remember their lawless deeds and exact punishment for their sins.

I found Israel like grapes in the wilderness, and I saw their fathers like a lookout in an early-ripening fig tree. They entered Baal-peor and estranged themselves in their shame, and the abominable things became like their beloved ones.
Ephraim flew away like a bird, and so did their glory from childbirth, labor pains, and pregnancy.
Even if they rear their children, they will be left childless among humankind. For woe to them! My flesh is from them.
As I saw Ephraim, they set their children out for the hunt, and Ephraim began to bring out his children for slaughter.
Give them, Lord—what will you give them? Give them a childless womb and dried-up breasts.
All their wickedness is in Gilgal, for there I hated them. Because of their evil conduct, I will drive them out of my house, and I will no longer love them. All their rulers are rebels.
Ephraim’s roots became diseased and dried up, and they will no longer bear fruit. Even if they give birth, I will take away the cherished children of their wombs.
God will reject them because they did not listen to him, and they will be wanderers among the nations.
Israel is a spreading, fruitful vine. According to the abundance of his fruit, he multiplied altars; according to the fertility of their land, they erected sacred pillars.
They divided their hearts; now they will be destroyed. He will overthrow their altars, and their sacred pillars will be ruined.
For now they will say, “We have no king, because we did not fear the Lord. But what could a king do for us?”
If he speaks words, they are pretexts for falsehood. He will make a covenant, and judgments will spring up like couch grass in the fallow ground of a field. For the calf of Beth-aven—
And the inhabitants of Samaria will become exiles, for its people mourned over it. And just as they embittered it, they will be trampled because of its glory, for that glory was carried away from it.
And they will take it bound to Assyria as an offering to King Jareb. He will receive Ephraim with bribes; Israel will be ashamed of its counsel.
Samaria rejected its king like a twig on the surface of the water.
The shrines of Aven, the sin of Israel, will be removed. Thorns and thistles will grow on their altars, and they will say to the mountains, “Fall on us,” and to the hills, “Cover us.”
Ever since the heights [?], Israel has sinned; there they took their stand. Let war not reach them on the heights; it came upon the sons of lawlessness.
To discipline them; and nations will gather against them to discipline them for their two injustices.
Ephraim is a trained heifer that loves opposition. But I will come upon her beautiful neck. I will mount Ephraim, and I will neglect Judah, and Jacob will grow strong against him.
Sow righteousness for yourselves and reap the fruit of life. Make the light of knowledge shine for yourselves. Seek the Lord until the fruits of righteousness come to you.
Why did you [?] wickedness and [?] its lawless deeds? You ate the fruit of falsehood, because you trusted in your chariots, in the greatness of your strength.

Destruction will arise against your people, and all your fortified places will be demolished, as the ruler Shalman from the house of Jerubbaal: on the day of battle they struck down the mother along with her children.
They will do the same to you, house of Israel, because of your evils. They fell at dawn; the king of Israel fell.
For Israel was a child, and I loved him, and I called my son out of Egypt.
As I called them, so they turned away from my presence. They sacrificed to the Baals and burned incense to carved images.
And I restrained Ephraim and took him into my arms, but they did not know that I was healing them.
I drew them away from human corruption with the bonds of my love, and I became to them like someone who strikes his jaw with a slap. I will look toward him and prevail over him.
Ephraim lived in Egypt, and the Assyrian was his king, because they did not want to return.
And he grew weak by the sword in his cities, and it ceased in his hands, and they will eat from their own counsels.
And his people will hang suspended from his dwelling, and God will be angry with his honored ones and will not raise them up.

How shall I deal with you, Ephraim? Rather, I will be your protector, Israel. How shall I deal with you? Shall I make you like Admah and like Zeboiim? My heart turned within itself; my compassion was stirred.
I will not act according to my fierce anger, and I will not allow Ephraim to be destroyed, for I am God and not a human being, the Holy One in your midst, and I will not enter your city.
Rather, I will walk after the Lord. He will roar like a lion, for he himself will roar and make the sons of the waters foolish.
They will fly and come like a bird from Egypt and like doves from the land of the Assyrians, and I will shelter them in their own houses, says the Lord.
Ephraim surrounded me with falsehood, and the house of Israel with ungodliness. As for Judah, God has now known them, and they will be called God's holy people.
But Ephraim is an evil wind; he pursued the scorching wind. All day long he increased vanity and empty things. He made a covenant with the Assyrians and carried oil to Egypt.
And the Lord has a judgment against Judah, and will seek vengeance on Jacob according to his ways; according to his conduct he will repay him.
In the womb he deceived his brother, and in his struggles he grew strong against God.
And he persevered against the angel and prevailed. They wept and sought me, and they found me in my house; there it was told to them.
And may the Lord God Almighty be their memorial.
And you shall return to your God, keep mercy and justice, and draw near to the Lord your God at all times.
A dishonest balance is in Canaan’s hand, and he loved to overpower others.
And Ephraim said, “I have become great; I have found rest for myself.” May none of his labors be found to his credit, because he transgressed through lawless deeds.
But I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of the Egyptians. I will make you dwell in tents again, as in the days of the festivals.
And I spoke to the prophets, and I multiplied visions, and through the prophets I will be represented.
If Gilead did not exist, then the rulers in Gilgal who offered sacrifices were false, and their altars were like heaps in a fallow field.
And Jacob went to the plain of the Syrians, and Israel served for a wife, and for a wife he kept watch.
And through the prophet the Lord brought Israel out of the land of the Egyptians, and through a prophet he was preserved.
Israel made me angry and provoked me, and his blood shall be poured out upon him. The Lord will repay him for his insults.
According to Ephraim’s words, he received the ordinances of the God of Israel, and assigned them to Baal and died.

And now they continued to sin and made cast images for themselves from their silver, in the likeness of idols, the work of craftsmen, to dedicate to them. And they say, “Sacrifice people, because the calves have run out.”
Therefore they shall be like a morning cloud and like the early dew that passes away, like dust swept from a threshing floor, and like smoke from windows.

I am the Lord your God, who established the heavens and established the earth, whose hands established all the hosts of heaven. I did not instruct you to follow them, and I brought you out of the land of the Egyptians. You shall know no God besides me, and there is no Savior besides me.
I tended you in the wilderness, in an uninhabited land.
They ate their fill from their pasture and took delight, and their hearts grew proud. Therefore they forgot me.
And I will be to them like a leopard and like a panther on the road of the Assyrians.
I will meet them like a hungry bear and tear open the covering of their hearts. The young lions of the forest will devour them, and wild beasts will tear them apart.
In your destruction, Israel, who will help you?
Where is your king? Let him save you in all your cities and give you justice—the one of whom you said, “Give me a king and a ruler.”
I gave you a king in my anger and cut him off in my wrath.
Ephraim is a bundle of unrighteous deeds; his sins lie hidden.
Pains like those of a woman giving birth will come upon him. This is your wise son; therefore he will not now be able to remain still when children break forth.
I will rescue them from the power of Hades and redeem them from death. Where is your victory, death? Where are your stings, Hades? Consolation is hidden from my eyes.

For he will cause division among his brothers. The Lord will bring upon him a scorching wind from the wilderness, and it will dry up his streams and destroy his springs. It will dry up his land and all his precious vessels.
Samaria will be destroyed because she rebelled against her God. They will fall by the sword, their nursing infants will be dashed against the rock, and their pregnant women will be ripped open.
Return, Israel, to the Lord your God, for you have grown weak through your lawless deeds.

Take words with you and return to the Lord your God, and say to him, “You can forgive our sins, so that we may not take on injustice, but you may accept good things, and we will offer in return the fruit of our lips.” And let your hearts enjoy goodness.
The Assyrian will not save us, and we will not ride horses. We will no longer call the works of our hands our God, for the one who is in you will have mercy on orphans.
I will heal their dwellings and love them all, for my anger has turned away from them.
I will be like dew to Israel, and he will blossom like a lily and spread his root like Lebanon.
His branches will spread, and he will be like an olive tree laden with fruit, and his fragrance will spread like frankincense.
They will return and dwell under his roof. They will live and be strengthened by grain, and he will blossom like a vine. His remembrance will be like the wine of Lebanon for Ephraim.
What more does he have to do with idols? I humbled him, and I will strengthen him. I am like a [?] vineyard; from me fruit was found in you.

Who is wise and will understand these things, discerning and will recognize these things? For the ways of the Lord are straight, and the righteous will walk in them, but the ungodly will falter in them.
